subject: math
explanation: When raising a power to another power, multiply the exponents: (nᵃ)ᵇ = nᵃˣᵇ. For example, (2³)² = 2⁶ = 64 because (2³)² = 2³ × 2³. Similarly, (13⁻²)⁻³ = 13⁶. This law helps rewrite large expressions compactly: 8⁶ can be written as (2³)⁶ = 2¹⁸ or (2²)⁹ = 2¹⁸. It is one of the most useful shortcuts when simplifying nested exponents.

brainstorming.question: Why multiply exponents in (nᵃ)ᵇ?
brainstorming.answer: nᵃ repeated b times means a × b total factors of n.

brainstorming.question: What does (n⁻²)⁻³ become?
brainstorming.answer: Multiply exponents: n⁽⁻²⁾ˣ⁽⁻³⁾ = n⁶ — negative × negative is positive.

misconceptions.correct: That is the product law. Power of a power multiplies: nᵃˣᵇ.

realLifeConnections.title: Nested scaling
realLifeConnections.description: Scaling by 10² then cubing the scale factor gives (10²)³ = 10⁶ overall magnification.

realLifeConnections.title: Fractal repetition

realLifeConnections.title: Cryptography layers
realLifeConnections.description: Applying a square operation twice on a key space can be modelled as a power of a power.

realLifeConnections.title: Volume of cubes
realLifeConnections.description: (side²)³ relates to expressing volume using power-of-a-power when side is itself a power.

realLifeConnections.title: Rewriting 64³
realLifeConnections.description: 64³ = (2⁶)³ = 2¹⁸ — compact form for very large numbers.

activities.title: Bracket challenge
activities.instructions: Compare (3²)⁴ and 3²⁴. Compute both and discuss why parentheses change the answer.

activities.title: Power tower simplify
activities.instructions: Simplify (5²)³, (2⁻¹)⁴, and (10³)² using the multiply-exponents rule.

activities.title: Two ways same answer
activities.instructions: Write 8⁶ as both (2³)⁶ and (2²)⁹. Verify both equal 2¹⁸.
